found.quote: Generative AI should always be used to support learning and academic integrity in line with IADT’s values and standards, and with the conceptual underpinning stated above.
When these (or any other tools) are utilised for the creation of academic work, they must be acknowledged and documented.
This may include citing the specific tool (and version) used, along with additional content such as prompts used and the process followed.
If the assessment specifically allows for the use of Generative AI tools, students are required to cite the tool’s contribution to their work.
Students must be informed of the purpose, process and ramifications of Generative AI tool use in assessment practice.
Be aware of bias and inaccuracy in the outputs of these tools.
When incorporating these tools into teaching and learning, issues of inequity and access must be considered.
Generative AI is an evolving suite of tools and these guidelines should be revisited at regular intervals.
Open discussion with students and staff regarding the inclusion/exclusion of these tools is encouraged.
Innovation in fair usage and ethical experimentation with Generative AI tools are encouraged by the institute in all disciplines to support and empower learners.
Include in assessment tasks processes designed to test for academic misconduct e.g. assessment panels, oral examination, project presentations
Student has right to appeal the decision to their Head of Department
plagiarism, cheating in any forum or form, cheating by way of falsification or fabrication, contract cheating

unsure.quote: Students are ultimately responsible for their learning and the work they submit.
unsure.why: General responsibility, not explicitly about AI content.

unsure.quote: It is important that students submit work that they have produced and acknowledge the sources used
unsure.why: Quoted NAIN principle, not an imperative about AI output.

unsure.quote: Inadvertent academic misconduct can be avoided by understanding academic techniques such as referencing, appropriate citation methods, adhering to the assessment brief, attending classes, etc.
unsure.why: Brief adherence mentioned generally, not as AI instruction.

unsure.quote: Engaging in discussions with lecturers about how academic integrity can be maintained
unsure.why: Discussion with lecturers, not about AI permission doubt.

unsure.quote: Be aware of the licenses associated with the output of Generative AI tools
unsure.why: Licensing awareness, ownership concern only implied.

unsure.quote: Students are advised to document the process of their work and how they arrived at the outputs submitted.
unsure.why: Process documentation advised, AI records not explicit.

unsure.quote: Please reference the Academic Misconduct Protocol (Appendix 2) in conjunction with this document.
unsure.why: Protocol general; AI cases not explicitly routed.

unsure.quote: Using the IADT Library (particularly LibGuides on Referencing) and Learning Support Services to help them with their work, where appropriate.
Inappropriate use of Generative AI tools without express permission from lecturer
unsure.why: Penalty-table example, not a stated general default.
